What is the best AI video generator when you count quality and cost?

Among the nine models this site tracks, Wan 3.0 has the highest published text-to-video Elo on AA-Video-T2V v2.1: 1174 ±13, rank range 1–2. That range overlaps Utopai X, which we do not track. MiniMax H3 (768p) at 1159, Dreamina Seedance 2.5 at 1156, and Gemini Omni Flash 1.2 at 1151 also have overlapping 95% intervals, so this site does not treat those four as a settled 1–2–3–4 finish. Wan 3.0 is also the cheapest of that high-Elo group in our catalog, at $0.0167/s on a Higgsfield Ultra annual plan at 480p, audio not stated, if you use every credit you pay for. If you only want the lowest dollar figure, use the cheapest-by-model guide instead.

Artificial Analysis’s pricing footnote says its $/minute column is the model creator’s API cost for one minute at the settings they benchmark (1080p where offered). This site does not use that column for ranking. Our dollar-per-second figures are the catalog rows above, each with a vendor URL.

How do you measure cost?

Every dollar-per-second figure is the cheapest current catalog row we track for that model, with its platform, plan or API, variant, resolution, audio, and rate label. Credit-plan figures assume you use every credit you pay for. A fal promo for MiniMax H3 Max Turbo ended November 15, 2026, so this guide uses the standard fal rate that the vendor page says resumes November 16, plus a cheaper Hailuo 2.3 plan estimate that is not the H3 leaderboard row.

Which model is best for each use?

For the highest published text-to-video quality among models we track, and the best value in that high-Elo group: Wan 3.0. For image-to-video quality: Seedance 2.5 leads AA-Video-I2V v2.1, but it is the most expensive model we track. For a cheaper high-Elo alternative: MiniMax H3 or Gemini Omni Flash 1.2, whose intervals overlap Wan 3.0’s neighbors. For a low-cost draft: Grok Imagine 1.5 Lite in the catalog at a lower Elo. For a model with no public Elo: Runway Gen-4 and Wan 3.0 Prime are unknown on the boards we opened, so this page does not rank them on quality.

How do we calculate this?

Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page (https://vidfare.com/about/).
